items.title: [decode-uri-component] decode-uri-component vulnerable to denial of service via quadratic replacement of percent-encoded runs
items.summary: SummarydecodeUriComponent() takes quadratic time on malformed input that has many distinct percent-encoded runs. A single unauthenticated request of about 224 KB can block the Node.js event loop for about 20 seconds. Version 0.5.0, the release that fixed CVE-2026-45822, is affected.DetailsWhen native decodeURIComponent throws, decodeUriComponent() falls back to customDecodeURIComponent (index.js:122). That function:Scans the input for every run of percent-encoded bytes (e.g. %C3%A5) and stores each distinct run, with its decoded value, in a lookup table (index.js:130-144).Runs one full-string input.replace(new RegExp(key, 'g'), …) per table entry (index.js:154).With K distinct runs in an input of length L, that's K regex compilations and K full scans of the string, so O(K·L). An attacker controls both K and L, and K grows with L. One malformed sequence such as a trailing %zz is enough to force the fallback path.The 0.5.0 fix for CVE-2026-45822 (fa479da) replaced the recursive decode() routine with a linear scanner, but left this replacement loop unchanged.Proof of conceptRunning the following code takes ~20 seconds.import decodeUriComponent from 'decode-uri-component';let payload = '';for (let i = 0; i < 32000; i++) {    const high = Math.floor(i / 256).toString(16).padStart(2, '0');    const low = (i % 256).toString(16).padStart(2, '0');    payload += `%${high}%${low}x`; // distinct run each iteration}payload += '%zz'; // forces the fallback decoderconsole.time('decode');decodeUriComponent(payload); // ~224 KBconsole.timeEnd('decode');ImpactThis is an availability issue only and there's no confidentiality or integrity impact. Any application that passes untrusted input to decodeUriComponent(), directly or through a dependency such as query-string, can be made unresponsive. Because Node.js runs on one thread, one request stalls every other client.The worst case needs input well beyond URL length limits. Node's default 16 KB header limit keeps payloads passed in via a URL query string to roughly 40 ms per request. Applications that decode request bodies are fully exposed, for example form bodies parsed with query-string.parse().Referenceshttps://github.com/SamVerschueren/decode-uri-component/security/advisories/GHSA-qr28-fpjm-wq7fhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-118664https://github.com/SamVerschueren/decode-uri-component/commit/fad01d65b93bd3f2f0dc32dfd8d57a38b57bc608https://github.com/SamVerschueren/decode-uri-component/releases/tag/v0.5.1https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qr28-fpjm-wq7f

items.title: [vite] Vite: `server.fs.deny` bypassed with queries
items.summary: SummaryThe contents of files that are specified by server.fs.deny can be returned to the browser. This is the same as https://github.com/vitejs/vite/security/advisories/GHSA-v2wj-q39q-566r.ImpactOnly apps that match the following conditions are affected:explicitly exposes the Vite dev server to the network (using --host or server.host config option)the sensitive file exists in the allowed directories specified by server.fs.allowthe sensitive file is denied with a pattern that matches a file by server.fs.denyDetailsOn the Vite dev server, files that should be blocked by server.fs.deny (e.g., .env, *.crt) can be retrieved with HTTP 200 responses when query parameters such as ?raw, ?import&raw, or ?import&url&inline are appended.For the fix for https://github.com/vitejs/vite/security/advisories/GHSA-rq7h-c2jc-7f22, v6.4.4 back-ported https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/20410. But while that PR requires https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/22160 for https://github.com/vitejs/vite/security/advisories/GHSA-v2wj-q39q-566r, https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/22160 wasn't back-ported together causing v6 vulnerable to https://github.com/vitejs/vite/security/advisories/GHSA-v2wj-q39q-566r.Referenceshttps://github.com/vitejs/vite/security/advisories/GHSA-8g5g-mxqh-grgjhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-118662https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/22160https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/23855https://github.com/vitejs/vite/commit/91e40d7bf9777057bbd31c3eb036a54c9465697ehttps://github.com/vitejs/vite/releases/tag/v6.4.5https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8g5g-mxqh-grgj

items.title: [@eeacms/volto-chatbot] @eeacms/volto-chatbot has Unauthenticated Danswer API Confused Deputy Proxy
items.summary: Unauthenticated Danswer API Confused Deputy Proxy in @eeacms/volto-chatbotSummary@eeacms/volto-chatbot exposes an Express middleware route (**/_v1_da/**) that accepts unauthenticated HTTP requests from any network client and proxies them to the configured upstream Danswer API, automatically attaching the server-side service credentials (DANSWER_API_KEY or session cookie). Because no authorization check, path allowlist, or method restriction is applied before the upstream request is issued, an unauthenticated attacker can invoke arbitrary Danswer API operations — including privileged admin endpoints — as the configured service account. This is a classic Confused Deputy attack: the Volto proxy acts as a deputy that carries credentials on behalf of the attacker.DetailsThe vulnerability is introduced across two source files in @eeacms/volto-chatbot@2.0.3.Route registration (src/index.js:15):middleware.all('**/_v1_da/**', proxyMiddleware);The wildcard pattern matches every HTTP method and any sub-path, and no authentication middleware is chained before proxyMiddleware. This means all requests reaching any /_v1_da/ path are forwarded without any identity check.Unvalidated path extraction and upstream URL construction (src/middleware.js:228-230):const path = req.url.replace('/_v1_da/', '/');const reqUrl = `${process.env.DANSWER_URL || ''}/api${path}`;The attacker-controlled req.url is transformed into the upstream Danswer path with a simple string replace. There is no allowlist of permitted paths, no restriction on HTTP methods, and no validation of the resulting URL. The attacker therefore fully controls which Danswer endpoint is called and with which HTTP method.Credential attachment and forwarding (src/middleware.js:164, src/middleware.js:169, src/middleware.js:202):// Session-cookie path (line 164):headers = { Cookie: cached_auth_cookie, ... }// API-key path (line 169):Authorization: 'Bearer ' + api_key,// Sink — final upstream dispatch (line 202):const response = await fetch(url, options, req.body);After constructing the URL from attacker-supplied input, the middleware attaches the server-side Danswer credentials (either a cached login session cookie or a Bearer API key) and dispatches the request. The response from Danswer is then relayed back to the unauthenticated client.Complete data flow (source → sink):src/index.js:15 — all **/_v1_da/** paths registered to proxyMiddleware with no auth guard (source: external HTTP request).src/middleware.js:228 — req.url used directly to derive the upstream path without allowlist.src/middleware.js:230 — attacker-controlled path appended to ${DANSWER_URL}/api.src/middleware.js:164 / src/middleware.js:169 — server-side session cookie or API key attached.src/middleware.js:202 — fetch(url, options, req.body) sends the fully-credentialed request to the Danswer backend (sink).This vulnerability is present whenever the add-on middleware is installed and DANSWER_API_KEY or DANSWER_USERNAME/DANSWER_PASSWORD is configured — conditions required for normal, documented operation of the package.PoCThe following steps reproduce the vulnerability using the Docker-based test harness provided with this report.Prerequisites:Docker installedPython 3 with the requests libraryStep 1 — Build the Docker image (from the npmAI_719_eea__volto-chatbot/ parent directory):docker build \  -f vuln-001/Dockerfile \  -t vuln001-proxy \  reports/npmAI_719_eea__volto-chatbotThe image packages the unmodified src/middleware.js from @eeacms/volto-chatbot@2.0.3, a minimal Express server that wires the vulnerable middleware, and an in-container mock Danswer server that echoes every received request as JSON. The environment variable DANSWER_API_KEY=supersecret is set to simulate a real deployment.Step 2 — Start the container:docker run --rm -d -p 3000:3000 --name vuln001-test vuln001-proxyThis launches both the Volto proxy (port 3000) and the mock Danswer server (port 18080) inside the container.Step 3 — Run the PoC exploit script:python3 vuln-001/poc.py 127.0.0.1 3000What the script does:Waits for the proxy to accept TCP connections.Sends an unauthenticated POST request with a JSON body to the admin-only Danswer endpoint via the proxy:POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/_v1_da/admin/users/deleteContent-Type: application/json{"id": "victim-user-123"}No Authorization or Cookie header is sent by the client.Expected output (exploit confirmed):[+] === EXPLOIT CONFIRMED — PASS ===[+] Decisive evidence:    1. Attacker-controlled path reached upstream : url='/api/admin/users/delete'    2. Server-side API key forwarded (no client auth) : authorization='Bearer supersecret'    3. Attacker-controlled HTTP method forwarded : method='POST'The mock Danswer server receives POST /api/admin/users/delete with Authorization: Bearer supersecret — proving that the attacker controlled both the upstream path and the HTTP method while the server silently attached its own credentials.Equivalent manual curl command (without Docker):# Terminal 1 —

items.title: [@cedar-policy/cedar-wasm] Cedar: JSON template is in scope missing slot-id validation allows link panic and decision divergence
items.summary: Cedar users must be using all of the following features to be affected by this advisory: JSON format policies, policy templates, and the is in scope condition. This advisory only affects JSON-formatted Cedar policy templates containing is in scope conditions that are malformed according to the Cedar syntax. It does not affect syntactically well-formed policies.Users of Cedar who author policies in the JSON format were able to write Cedar policies using the is in condition with an incorrect slot identifier in the principal and resource scope constraints (e.g., ?principal in the resource scope constraint) even though this is not allowed when parsing policies from the Cedar policy syntax. Internally, the slot identifiers were silently corrected (e.g. ?resource is placed in the resource scope constraint). If the policy contains exactly one slot in either the principal or resource position, then any attempt to create a linked policy from the template results in an error: the internal representation of the template does not contain the slot identifier as written in the malformed JSON policy (it has been corrected silently), so attempting to fill that slot is an error. If instead the template is linked using slot identifier expected internally (i.e., not what is written in the JSON template), the linking will initially succeed, but a subsequent invariant violation will cause a panic.When the template contains slots in both the principal and resource position, then both slots will be present in the internal representation: linking succeeds, but with each slot bound to the value intended for the other (the silent correction). The linked policy is then semantically different from the malformed policy the user intended, and any subsequent authorization decision made against that policy may lead to accesses being unintentionally allowed or denied.Concretely, consider the following JSON format policy template intended to deny users in a particular project from accessing documents with a particular classification.{  "effect": "forbid",  "principal": {    "op": "is",    "entity_type": "User",    "in": { "slot": "?resource" }  },  "action": { "op": "All" },  "resource": {    "op": "is",    "entity_type": "Doc",    "in": { "slot": "?principal" }  },  "conditions": []}Linked with ?principal = Classification::"topsecret" and ?resource = Project::"alpha", the author expects to create the policy:forbid(principal is User in Project::"alpha", action, resource is Doc in Classification::"topsecret");But because Cedar internally links slots by scope position (not by name), the actual policy evaluated by the engine is:forbid(principal is User in Classification::"topsecret", action, resource is Doc in Project::"alpha");If a user is in Project::"alpha" but not Classification::"topsecret", the forbid policy does not apply, and access is unintentionally allowed.PatchesThis advisory is patched in version 4.11.1 and 3.4.3, both available on Crates.io and NPM.WorkaroundsIf you cannot update to a patched version, you can determine if you are affected by checking your JSON format policy templates for the following two patterns.  "principal": {    "op": "is",    "entity_type": "User",    "in": { "slot": "?resource" }  }and  "resource": {    "op": "is",    "entity_type": "Doc",    "in": { "slot": "?principal" }  }ReferencesCedar Policy Language Reference Guide - Cedar Policy TemplatesCedar Policy Language Reference Guide - JSON Policy FormatReferenceshttps://github.com/cedar-policy/cedar/security/advisories/GHSA-c33x-vcv4-vg3ghttps://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c33x-vcv4-vg3g

items.title: [@sylphx/pdf-reader-mcp] @sylphx/pdf-reader-mcp: HTTP transport accepts unauthenticated requests despite a configured MCP_API_KEY
items.summary: ImpactWhen @sylphx/pdf-reader-mcp is run as an HTTP server (MCP_TRANSPORT=http), it reads the MCP_API_KEY environment variable and logs API key authentication enabled (X-API-Key header) at startup, but it never validated the X-API-Key header on incoming requests. The key was read into a variable and never enforced on the request path.As a result, the /mcp endpoint accepted unauthenticated requests. Combined with the default bind address of 0.0.0.0 (all interfaces), any client able to reach the port could invoke every PDF tool and read the contents of any PDF the server process could open anywhere on the host. URL-based sources also enable limited SSRF (private/loopback addresses are blocked by default unless --allow-private-ips is set).The misleading startup log made the exposure silent: an operator who set MCP_API_KEY reasonably believed the server was protected when it was not.This affects only the opt-in HTTP transport; the default stdio transport is unaffected.PatchesFixed in @sylphx/pdf-reader-mcp@3.0.1. The fix enforces the X-API-Key header with a constant-time comparison (rejecting missing/mismatched keys with HTTP 401), changes the default bind host to 127.0.0.1 (loopback), and emits a startup warning when binding a non-loopback host without an API key.WorkaroundsFor deployments that cannot upgrade immediately:Bind to loopback only: MCP_HTTP_HOST=127.0.0.1.Place a reverse proxy in front that enforces authentication.Use the default stdio transport instead of HTTP.Restrict filesystem reach with --allow-dir / MCP_PDF_ALLOWED_DIRS.Reported privately by novice-22 via responsible disclosure.Referenceshttps://github.com/SylphxAI/pdf-reader-mcp/security/advisories/GHSA-q344-5v34-gm84https://github.com/SylphxAI/anymd/pull/332https://github.com/SylphxAI/anymd/commit/4c35f72862d729301e3912ab8c8317d2828cf4c2https://github.com/SylphxAI/anymd/releases/tag/v3.0.1https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-q344-5v34-gm84

items.title: [parse-server] Parse Server vulnerable to stored XSS via malformed Content-Type bypassing file upload extension blocklist
items.summary: ImpactParse Server's file upload validation uses the fileUpload.fileExtensions option (enabled by default with a blocklist) to reject files that browsers may render as active content, mitigating stored cross-site scripting (XSS). When an uploaded file's extension is not recognized by the mime package, Parse Server preserves the client-supplied Content-Type and passes it to the storage adapter. A malformed Content-Type that is not a valid type/subtype media type — for example image (no subtype), image/ (empty subtype), or image//svg+xml (invalid token) — bypassed the blocklist and was stored unchanged. On storage adapters that persist and serve the uploaded Content-Type (such as Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage, or Azure Blob Storage), a browser cannot parse the malformed Content-Type and falls back to MIME-sniffing the file content; a file whose body begins with HTML markup is then rendered as HTML, executing any embedded script in the application's origin. This allows a user permitted to upload files to store content that executes as script against other users who open the file URL. The default GridFS storage adapter is not affected, as it recomputes the Content-Type from the filename and serves files with X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.PatchesThe file upload handler now validates that the client-supplied Content-Type is a well-formed media type (type/subtype with non-empty tokens per RFC 9110 §5.6.2) whenever the filename extension is not recognized by mime. Malformed values are rejected instead of being stored, while well-formed types — including custom or vendor types that the mime package does not recognize — continue to be accepted; only blocklisted subtypes are rejected.WorkaroundsConfigure fileUpload.fileExtensions as a strict allowlist of only the extensions the application needs (for example ["^(png|jpe?g|gif|pdf)$"]). Additionally, serve uploaded files from a domain separate from the application so that any rendered content is isolated from the application's origin, and configure the storage/CDN layer to send X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.ReferencesGitHub security advisory: https://github.com/parse-community/parse-server/security/advisories/GHSA-r899-h629-j84rFix Parse Server 9: https://github.com/parse-community/parse-server/pull/10521Fix Parse Server 8: https://github.com/parse-community/parse-server/pull/10523Referenceshttps://github.com/parse-community/parse-server/security/advisories/GHSA-r899-h629-j84rhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-61448https://www.vulncheck.com/advisories/parse-server-stored-xss-via-malformed-content-typehttps://github.com/advisories/GHSA-r899-h629-j84r
